'''Holdyn Jerian Grant''' (born October 9, 1992) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his senior season with the [[University of Notre Dame]].  He is considered one of the top college players in the nation for the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]].

==College career==
After a high school career at prep power [[DeMatha Catholic High School]], Grant came to Notre Dame to play for coach [[Mike Brey]].  After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his freshman season,<ref name=SUSP>{{cite web | last = Dauster | first = Rob | title = The maturation of Jerian Grant: What one star learned during a season-long suspension | work = NBCSports.com | date = November 13, 2014 | url = http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/13/the-maturation-jerian-grant-what-one-star-learned-during-a-season-long-suspension/ | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref> Grant was named to the [[Big East Conference]] All-Rookie team after averaging 12.3 points and 4.97 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Jack Cooley And Jerian Grant Named To BIG EAST All-Conference Teams | work = [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish]]| date = March 4, 2012 | url = http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030412aaa.html | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref> In his second season with the Irish, Grant was named second-team All-Big East after averaging 13.3 points and 5.5 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Cooley, Grant named to All-Big East teams  | work = [[Comcast SportsNet Chicago]] | date = March 10, 2013 | url = http://www.csnchicago.com/blog/irish-talk/cooley-grant-named-all-big-east-teams | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref>

After the 2012–13 season, Notre Dame moved from the Big East to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC).  Based on his strong sophomore campaign, Grant was voted onto the preseason All-ACC team.<ref>{{cite web | last = Murray | first = Jason | title = Syracuse's C.J. Fair voted ACC preseason player of the year; Orange picked to finish 2nd in league  | work = [[Syracuse.com]] | date = March 10, 2013 | url = http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/10/syracuse_forward_cj_fair_voted.html | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref>  Grant had a strong start to the season, leading the Fighting Irish at 19.0 points per game during their 8–4 start.  But on December 23, 2013 Grant was ruled academically ineligible for the rest of the season and forced to withdraw from Notre Dame.<ref>{{cite web | last = Fortuna | first = Matt | title = Notre Dame Loses Leading Scorer | work = [[ESPN.com]] | date = December 23, 2013 | url = http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10182486/academics-force-notre-dame-fighting-irish-leading-scorer-jerian-grant-leave-team | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref>  Grant chose to return to Notre Dame rather than declare his eligibility for the [[2014 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Hamilton | first = Brian | title = Jerian Grant returns from suspension to make Notre Dame relevant again | work = [[Sports Illustrated]] | date = September 4, 2014 | url = http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2014/09/04/jerian-grant-notre-dame-acc-suspension | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref> 

Grant returned to Notre Dame for the 2014–15 season.  Grant immediately helped the Fighting Irish to a 20–3 start and Grant personally had a breakout season as the leader of the team's highly efficient offense.<ref>{{cite web | last = Dauster | first = Rob | title = Film Session: The case for Jerian Grant as National Player of the Year | work = NBCSports.com | date = January 29, 2015 | url = http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/01/29/film-session-the-case-for-jerian-grant-as-national-player-of-the-year/ | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref>  He was named to the midseason watch lists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]] and the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Erickson | first = Nick | title = Wooden Award Midseason Top 25 list revealed | work = [[Washington Post]] | date = January 14, 2015 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2015/01/14/wooden-award-midseason-top-25-list-revealed/ | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Oscar Robertson Trophy Midseason Watch List Announced | work = [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] | date = January 23, 2015 | url = http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2015/oscar150123.html | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref> The Grant-led Irish finished the year with a 32-6 record and an ACC Tournament championship; they advanced to the Elite 8 in the Midwest Region, where they lost to an undefeated Kentucky team by 2 points.<ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Survived No. 1 Kentucky holds off Notre Dame 68-66 | date = March 28, 2015 | url = https://sports.yahoo.com/news/survived-no-1-kentucky-holds-off-notre-dame-031309800--ncaab.html | accessdate = March 28, 2015}}</ref>

==Personal==
Jerian Grant is the son of former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Harvey Grant]].  He has two brothers who play basketball professionally – oldest brother [[Jerai Grant|Jerai]] has played in several leagues around the world and younger brother [[Jerami Grant|Jerami]] plays in the NBA.  Youngest brother Jaelin has followed his three older brothers to DeMatha, where he is completing his senior season.  His uncle [[Horace Grant]] was an [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and won four championships with the [[Chicago Bulls]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Hamilton | first = Brian | title = Notre Dame's Jerian Grant raised on basketball | work = [[Chicago Tribune]] | date = February 2, 2012 | url = http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-02-02/sports/ct-spt-0203-notre-dame-basketball--20120203_1_dad-harvey-grant-basketball | accessdate = February 1, 2015}}</ref>
